items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6931

SPONSOR: PERALTA
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the vehicle and traffic law, in relation to requiring
the city of New York to establish a pilot residential parking permit
system within a two mile radius of LaGuardia airport; and providing for
the repeal of such provisions upon expiration thereof

 
PURPOSE:

Provides for the City of New York to adopt a residential parking permit
system in the borough of Queens. This pilot program would be zoned near
LaGuardia Airport.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

The bill amends the vehicle and traffic law by adding a new Section
1640-q, which would allow the city of New York, by adoption of local law
or ordinance, to provide for a one-year residential parking permit pilot
program.

The permit system would be zoned by the City of New York within the
borough of Queens, covering an area within a 2-mile radius of LaGuardia
Airport.

The City of New York would fix and require the payment of fees applica-
ble to parking within areas designated by the city of New York.

The bill provides that no permit will be required on streets where the
adjacent properties are zoned for commercial or retail use.

The bill provides that the permit zone shall make 20% of spaces avail-
able to non-residents, and short-term 90 minute parking will also be
made available.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Parking in New York City has always been difficult to find, but the
City's residents are affected the most. Due to New York City's populari-
ty as a tourist destination, sports city, and job hub, the City sees a
majority of its parking taken by commuters and people who are passing
through.

Residential parking permit programs have been implemented in major
cities such as Chicago, Baltimore, Atlanta, San Diego, Houston, and many
others. This legislation would allow New York City to implement a one-
year pilot program in an area of high need: the neighborhoods surround-
ing LaGuardia Airport. Not only have residents' parking been taken by
travelers and people commuting into the city, but the large workforce of
LaGuardia contributes heavily to the parking scarcity.

This one-year pilot will be administered by the City of New York, and
will only be implemented after a public hearing is held near the
proposed zone to hear from all who may be impacted.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New Bill

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None to the State

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
Immediately

summary: Requires the city of New York to establish a residential parking permit system in the borough of Queens within a two mile radius of LaGuardia airport.
